house_rule: Signals are read from the underlying index; option-chain data is context or a filter only. Solo is paper only, forever.

concepts.name: Open interest (OI) and OI change
concepts.what: The number of option (or futures) contracts still open at a strike: every contract has one buyer and one seller, so OI counts positions, not trades. OI rises when new positions open and falls when they close.
concepts.formula: Read directly from the chain for each strike and side. R61: near-the-money OI = call + put OI at the 5 strikes nearest the money (log10); OI change = % change of call + put OI at the 11 nearest strikes since the day's first chain minute; 'writer tilt' = put OI % change minus call OI % change over 30 minutes.
concepts.phone: yes: ChainAnalytics.oiData / oiProfile / oiChange from the live chain (Dhan or Zerodha)
concepts.use: Traders read rising OI as fresh conviction and falling OI as positions being closed. Big call-OI additions are read as call writing (a ceiling), big put-OI additions as put writing (a floor).
pitfalls: OI is published with a lag (NSE updates it every few minutes), so minute-level OI changes are stale.
You cannot tell from OI alone whether the buyer or the seller opened the position.
Lot-size changes and expiry roll-offs move OI without any view behind it.

research.sample: BANKNIFTY, two years (Feb 2024-Feb 2026), 145 arm x check results
research.finding: No OI or volume check improved the Liquidity arm in both years; the ORB 'volume surge' kept 3% of trades and never reached t = 2.

Put-minus-call OI change had a 15-minute IC of about 0.03, too small to pay costs (holdout -Rs 45 a day). The filter 'skip when the 15-minute OI build-up opposes the trade' (BU15): holdout +Rs 81 a day on 876 trades, p 0.035, pre-holdout q 0.13.
Futures OI rising as a daily filter: -Rs 9.4 a day, q 0.50.

concepts.name: OI build-up types
concepts.what: Price change and OI change read together: price up + OI up = long build-up (new buyers); price down + OI up = short build-up (new sellers); price up + OI down = short covering (sellers closing); price down + OI down = long unwinding (buyers closing).
concepts.formula: R61: the index's 30-minute change and the 30-minute change of call + put OI at the 11 strikes nearest the money: +2 long build-up, +1 short covering, -1 long unwinding, -2 short build-up, 0 if either is flat. Classic build-up uses FUTURES OI; the lake has index-futures minutes only from Jul 2026, so R61 uses near-the-money option OI instead.
concepts.phone: yes (option OI version); futures build-up from the futures quote stream (recorded from Jul 2026)
concepts.use: A trend is trusted when it comes with build-up on its side (long build-up for up moves) and doubted when it is only covering or unwinding.
pitfalls: It labels the past 30 minutes; it is a description, not a forecast.
Option OI mixes calls and puts and both buyers and writers; the labels come from futures.

research.finding: A fixed 'smart money' rule (puts written, calls covered, PCR rising) lost on all 5 indices (-Rs 24 to -245 a trade).
Futures build-up: lowest q 0.54; nothing survives.
Put long-unwinding share: 15-minute direction IC +0.029 ('barely').

concepts.name: Put-call ratio (PCR), on OI and on volume
concepts.what: Put OI divided by call OI (or put volume / call volume). Above 1: more puts than calls.
concepts.formula: R61: put / call OI at the 11 strikes nearest the money (A2 already uses this level); its change over 30 minutes; put / call volume summed since 09:15; and the rank of today's OI ratio among the last 5 and 20 sessions at the same minute.
concepts.phone: yes: ChainAnalytics.pcr (OI and volume); the ranks need the phone's own stored history of past sessions
concepts.use: Read both ways: as sentiment (many puts = fear, a contrarian buy) or as writing (many puts written = a floor, bullish). Extremes versus the index's own history matter more than the raw level.
pitfalls: The same number is read bullish by one school and bearish by another.
The ratio depends on which strikes are included and on the expiry; compare like with like.
Near expiry, OI shifts fast and the ratio swings without meaning.

concepts.name: Max pain
concepts.what: The expiry price at which option holders, taken together, would get the least money: the strike that minimises the total payout on all open calls and puts.
concepts.formula: For each chain strike X: sum over strikes K of call OI x max(X - K, 0) + put OI x max(K - X, 0); max pain = the X with the smallest total (ties: the lowest strike). R61: (max pain - index) / index x 100, signed by the trade's side, over the 21 strikes around the money.
concepts.phone: yes: ChainAnalytics.maxPain
concepts.use: Folklore says the index is 'pulled' toward max pain into expiry because option writers defend it.
pitfalls: It changes every minute as OI changes, and depends on the strike window used.
It assumes writers can move the index; our data says they do not.

research.finding: As a forecast of the expiry close, max pain is worse than 'no change': error 0.74% vs 0.43% (BANKNIFTY), 0.58% vs 0.52% (NIFTY).
The close ended 0.58% from max pain vs 0.50% from the open; within 0.25% of it on only 25% / 27% of expiries.
No drift toward max pain or max OI (BANKNIFTY -10 bps, t -2.2: if anything, away).

concepts.name: OI walls (support and resistance from OI)
concepts.what: The strike with the most call OI above the index (read as resistance) and with the most put OI below it (read as support).
concepts.formula: R61: % distance from the index to the biggest call-OI strike at or above it and to the biggest put-OI strike at or below it (ties: the nearer one), within the 21 strikes around the money; expressed as 'wall ahead' (on the trade's way) and 'wall behind'.
concepts.phone: yes: ChainAnalytics.oiProfile (max call / put OI strikes)
concepts.use: Option buyers avoid buying calls just under a big call wall; breakouts 'through a wall' are chased.
pitfalls: Walls move as OI shifts; a wall is only as strong as the writers' willingness to hold.
Far walls just mean the market expects a wide range.

research.finding: Max-OI strikes were neither walls nor magnets: 0 of 12 tests; the max-OI strike was closer to settlement than a random same-distance strike on 42-43% of expiries (no-magnet level about 44%).
OI walls as the breakout range: +1,745 design, -3,972 holdout; random levels did better in 6 of 7 variants.
OI-wall blast: -Rs 3,851; best p 0.73, every q 1.00. 'The OI part adds nothing.'

concepts.name: Implied volatility (IV), ATM IV
concepts.what: The volatility that makes the Black-Scholes price equal the option's market price: how much movement the market is paying for. Higher IV = dearer options.
concepts.formula: From the chain's IV column (the lake and the broker both give it per strike); ATM IV = mean of the at-the-money call and put IV. R61 adds its change since the day's first chain minute.
concepts.phone: yes: ChainAnalytics.ivSmile (ATM IV), broker IV per strike
concepts.use: Option buyers prefer cheap IV (less to lose if IV falls) and fear 'IV crush' after events; sellers like high IV.
pitfalls: A buyer can be right on direction and still lose when IV falls.
IV is quoted per expiry; weekly IV near expiry is noisy.
Bad ticks in thin strikes give absurd IVs (R61 removes them before use).

research.finding: Day range rose with opening IV: 464 / 540 / 631 points by IV third (83 days each). Descriptive.
Buying when IV is cheap versus a realised-vol forecast: best -Rs 30 a day net, q 0.80; 0 of 12 filters adopted.
In Solo 2.0, ATM IV is the largest negative weight (-0.21): dear options are skipped.

concepts.name: IV rank and IV percentile
concepts.what: Where today's IV sits in its own past: IV rank = (IV - lowest) / (highest - lowest) over a look-back; IV percentile = share of past days with lower IV.
concepts.formula: R61: ATM IV rank (min-max) among the previous 60 sessions at the same minute (needs 40 sessions; Boss's Nov 2024 data rule makes 252-day ranks too short to train on).
concepts.phone: partly: needs 60 sessions of the phone's own stored ATM IV; missing until then
concepts.use: Buy options when IV rank is low, sell when it is high.
pitfalls: One spike in the window squashes every later rank (min-max).
A short look-back mixes event weeks with quiet ones.

research.finding: BANKNIFTY calls when IV percentile is high: +Rs 12,319, p 0.02-0.03 but q 0.28, and it lost in design.
Buying straddles at low IV percentile loses.
IV percentile / rank are good SIZE predictors (IC about +0.23-0.24), not direction.

concepts.name: IV skew and smile
concepts.what: How IV differs across strikes. Skew: out-of-the-money puts usually carry higher IV than calls (crash insurance). Smile: both wings dearer than the middle.
concepts.formula: A2: put IV 3 strikes below minus call IV 3 strikes above (skew). R61 adds smile curvature = (put IV -3 + call IV +3) / 2 - ATM IV. 25-delta skew is NOT used: deltas of far strikes on a 21-strike chain are noisy; the +-3-strike version is the stated substitute.
concepts.phone: yes: ChainAnalytics.ivSmile
concepts.use: Steep put skew = demand for protection (fear); flattening skew = calm. Some read rising call skew as upside speculation.
pitfalls: Skew in points depends on the strike distance chosen and on IV level.
Thin far strikes give unreliable IVs.

research.finding: The one direction clue that pointed the same way everywhere: when puts are dearer, the index tends to rise over 30-60 minutes (IC +0.03 to +0.13 fit, +0.01 to +0.08 selection). Too small to pay costs.
Skew / synthetic-forward direction rules all lose (best -Rs 76 a day net).
A rule leaning on skew: +Rs 277 a trade, q 0.109; near-miss, in a forward test.

concepts.name: IV term structure
concepts.what: IV of the next expiry versus a later one. Normally later expiries carry slightly higher IV (contango); near-term IV above far-term (backwardation) signals near-term stress or an event.
concepts.formula: R61: NIFTY only, monthly-file ATM IV minus weekly-file ATM IV (0 when both are the same contract). For BANKNIFTY, FINNIFTY and MIDCPNIFTY there are only monthly expiries since 20 Nov 2024, so there is no second expiry in the lake to compare (missing).
concepts.phone: yes: ChainAnalytics.volSurface across expiries
concepts.use: Backwardation warns of an event or panic; option buyers prefer the expiry whose IV is relatively cheap.
pitfalls: Only exists while two expiries trade; the week of the monthly expiry collapses it.
Weekly IV jumps around expiry days by construction.

research.finding: Monthly minus weekly ATM IV 'did not sort the realised move at all'.
Crude term structure predicts nothing.

concepts.name: India VIX
concepts.what: NSE's index of NIFTY's expected volatility over the next 30 days, computed from NIFTY option prices (annualised %).
concepts.formula: Streamed as an index (INDIAVIX). A2 uses the level and the change from the previous close; R61 adds its rank among the previous 60 sessions at the same minute.
concepts.phone: yes: VIX stream / 1-minute bars (MarketRecorder)
concepts.use: High VIX = bigger expected moves and dearer options; spikes mark fear, falling VIX calm.
pitfalls: VIX is about NIFTY; other indices have their own IV.
It says how big, not which way.

research.finding: Skipping low-VIX days cost -Rs 73.4 a day (q 0.77): low-VIX days were good for the Liquidity arm.
VIX pointed the wrong way for ORB in one year (-8.9k) and the right way in the other.
VIX alone matches a model for the next day's and rest-of-day range (size IC +0.22).
VIX is A2's largest positive weight (+0.22).

concepts.name: Delta
concepts.what: How much the option's price moves for a 1-point move in the index (0 to 1 for calls, 0 to -1 for puts); also roughly the chance of expiring in the money.
concepts.formula: Black-Scholes: call N(d1), put N(d1) - 1, d1 = (ln(S/K) + (r + s^2/2) T) / (s sqrt T), from the contract's own IV; R61 uses r = 6.5% and T = (sessions to expiry + rest of today / 375) / 252.
concepts.phone: yes: ChainAnalytics / OptionMath Greeks
concepts.use: Pick strikes (ITM = higher delta, behaves like the index), size positions, convert an index view into option points.
pitfalls: Delta changes with the index (gamma), time and IV.
Model delta with a wrong IV or T misleads near expiry.

research.finding: Delta as a direction feature: IC about +0.012 (noise).
research.verdict: context only; never tested as a rule

concepts.name: Gamma
concepts.what: How fast delta changes as the index moves. High gamma (at the money, near expiry) = the option's exposure grows quickly in a move, both ways.
concepts.formula: Black-Scholes gamma = pdf(d1) / (S s sqrt T); R61 reports it as the change in delta for a 1% index move (gamma x S x 0.01).
concepts.phone: yes: OptionMath Greeks
concepts.use: Buyers like gamma for fast moves (expiry-day 'hero' trades); sellers fear it.
pitfalls: Gamma explodes in the last hours of expiry; small index moves swing the premium wildly.

research.finding: Gamma near the money predicts move SIZE (IC about +0.15), not direction.
0 of 52 pass.

concepts.name: Theta (time decay)
concepts.what: How much value the option loses per day if nothing else changes. Always a cost to the buyer; biggest at the money and near expiry.
concepts.formula: Black-Scholes theta per session (1/252 year); R61 reports it as % of the premium.
concepts.phone: yes: OptionMath Greeks
concepts.use: Buyers want the move to come before decay eats the premium; time stops exist because of theta.
pitfalls: Theta is not linear: the last day's decay is far bigger than the average day's.

research.finding: On expiry day the ATM option keeps a median 11% (NIFTY) / 19% (BANKNIFTY) of its 09:20 time value at 14:00, and 2% / 4% at 15:00. Descriptive.
Theta: size IC about +0.10.

concepts.name: Vega
concepts.what: How much the option's price moves for a 1-point change in IV.
concepts.formula: Black-Scholes vega = S pdf(d1) sqrt T / 100 per IV point; R61 reports it as % of the premium.
concepts.phone: yes: OptionMath Greeks
concepts.use: Buyers of long-dated or ATM options carry more vega: an IV drop (after an event) hurts them.
pitfalls: Weekly options have little vega; IV crush matters more for monthlies.

research.finding: Vega: direction IC about +0.01.

concepts.name: Gamma exposure (GEX) and the gamma-flip level
concepts.what: An estimate of how much option dealers must buy or sell the index to stay hedged as it moves. If dealers are long gamma (positive GEX) they sell rallies and buy dips (calmer market); short gamma (negative GEX) they chase moves (wilder market). The flip is the index level where net GEX changes sign.
concepts.formula: Net GEX = sum over strikes of (call gamma x call OI - put gamma x put OI) x S^2 x 0.01, assuming dealers are long calls and short puts (the convention R28 used). R61: net / gross (between -1 and +1), its sign, and the % distance to the level (within +-3%) where net GEX, re-priced, changes sign.
concepts.phone: yes: ChainAnalytics.gex / gammaDensity (note: the phone prices from the forward; a port must match R61's definition exactly)
concepts.use: Positive GEX: fade moves, expect ranges. Negative GEX / below the flip: expect trends and bigger moves.
pitfalls: In India we do not know who holds which side; the sign convention is an assumption (OF1: clients and Pros are net option writers).
GEX is strongly tied to IV (R36: correlation -0.69), so it mostly repeats what IV says.

research.finding: Negative GEX at 10:00 -> somewhat bigger rest-of-day range (BANKNIFTY 0.87% vs 0.75%); 0 of 10 arm filters passed; on the Night arm it cut the holdout from +249 to -18 a day.
research.verdict: size only; failed as a filter

research.finding: Correlation 0.33 with the afternoon move, but it is an IV effect; trades 0 of 4 pass, -Rs 1,03,781.
Trading the flip: -Rs 40,003, worse than 99.4% of random entries; 0 of 4 pass.
GEX sign flipped between periods; 0 of 28 pass.

concepts.name: Dealer positioning
concepts.what: Which group holds which side of the options book; GEX depends on it.
concepts.formula: Not observable directly. NSE's participant-wise OI (client, DII, FII, Pro; daily, after 18:30) is the closest public proxy.
concepts.phone: partly: MarketRecorder records the participant file daily; intraday positioning is not available
concepts.use: Traders assume writers (dealers) hedge and so pin or push the index.
pitfalls: Indian clients and Pros, not 'dealers', are the net writers (OF1: 97% / 92% of days).
Daily file only, a day late for intraday decisions.

research.finding: Follow-the-group signals: 15 of 36 passed on 2012-2025, then 0 of 15 held in the last 12 months (13 flipped sign).
'GEX sign / flip decides trend': inconsistent in our data.

concepts.r61_result: No R61 input: positioning is not observable intraday; participant OI (its proxy) is measured under 'FII / DII flows and participant-wise OI'.

concepts.name: VWAP
concepts.what: The average price of the day weighted by volume: where most of the day's trading happened.
concepts.formula: sum(price x volume) / sum(volume) from the open. The index itself has no volume, so A2 uses the typical-price average of the session ('dist_tpavg_pct') as the index proxy; true VWAP needs futures volume (futures minutes from Jul 2026 in the lake).
concepts.phone: partly: futures VWAP from the futures stream; the index has no volume
concepts.use: Above VWAP = buyers in control; pullbacks to VWAP are bought in up-trends.
pitfalls: On an index without volume, 'VWAP' is a different number in every app.

research.finding: 9 EMA + VWAP + HH/HL: every version loses or is flat.
'VWAP reject': best q 0.12; primary -Rs 1,505 a day in the holdout.
EMA + Supertrend + VWAP lost Rs 2.5-3.3 lakh in design and holdout.

concepts.role: context or filter only: may make Solo skip or prefer a candidate, never create a trade or pick its side
concepts.r61_result: Not a new R61 input (A2 already has the typical-price proxy `dist_tpavg_pct`); R61 did not test it again.

concepts.name: ATR (average true range)
concepts.what: The average daily (or bar) range including gaps: the index's normal move size.
concepts.formula: True range = max(high - low, |high - previous close|, |low - previous close|); ATR14 = mean of the last 14 completed days. A2 uses daily ATR14 as % of price; SoloMidday's stops are in ATR.
concepts.phone: yes: from index candles
concepts.use: Scale stops and targets to the market's current movement.
pitfalls: Lags: after a quiet spell a sudden move is far bigger than ATR.

research.finding: ATR is the strongest SIZE predictor (IC +0.335); direction is noise.
ATR-adaptive ranges and range-scaled stops were no better.

concepts.role: size/context only: our research says it predicts how much the index may move, not which way
concepts.r61_result: Not a new R61 input (A2 already has `atr14d_pct`); R61 did not test it again.

concepts.name: Opening range
concepts.what: The high and low of the first minutes of the session (15 or 30); a break above or below is read as the day's direction.
concepts.phone: yes: from index minutes
concepts.use: Buy the breakout side, stop at the other side.
pitfalls: Most breaks fail or reverse in a range day; costs eat the small wins.

research.finding: ORB: -Rs 2,23,040; 0 of 6 years profitable; 0 of 16 versions pass.
Still loses.
S4 (15-min ORB) unfiltered: -Rs 1,14,070.

concepts.role: a candidate setup (S4, signal on the index) and a context feature
concepts.r61_result: Not a new R61 input (A2 has `or30_state`; S4 is a candidate setup). In R61's final test the 15-minute ORB setup was almost never taken (0-2 trades per variant).

concepts.name: Value area / market profile
concepts.what: Market profile counts how long price spent at each level (time-price opportunities). POC = the most traded level; the value area holds 70% of the day's activity (VAH top, VAL bottom).
concepts.formula: Previous day's 30-minute TPO profile, 70% value area (h37 sigs.profile_levels). R61: (index - previous POC) / (VAH - VAL), signed by the trade's side.
concepts.phone: yes: from index minutes
concepts.use: Opening outside yesterday's value and staying there = trend day ('open outside value and go'); inside value = range.
pitfalls: Many ways to build a profile (bin size, TPO period); results depend on them.

research.finding: 'Open outside value and go' (S3) made +Rs 49,360 unfiltered in the final window; A2 took 92 of its 128 trades from it. R52 chose its exit on this same window, so it is not fresh.
HVNs and the POC turn price no more often than placebo levels; auction rules 0 of 56.
TPO-based rules among them: SPA p 1.00.

concepts.role: a candidate setup (S3, signal on the index) and a context feature
concepts.r61_result: R61 (15 Oct 2026; design walk-forward Jul 2025 - Mar 2026 on 5,780 candidate rows, final 1 Apr - 14 Oct 2026, not fresh): removing the 'value area' inputs from the all-inputs model changed walk-forward AUC by +0.0007 (design) / -0.0002 (final) and net by Rs -1,001 / Rs -3,439. Each input added alone to A2's 29 changed AUC (design / final): `va_pos` -0.0019 / -0.0005. Verdict: no measurable help out of sample (every AUC change under 0.01; the net changes go both ways and are within what one or two trades swing).

concepts.name: Trend vs range regimes
concepts.what: Whether the market is trending (moves far for its distance travelled) or ranging (back and forth).
concepts.formula: Efficiency ratio = |net move| / sum of |bar moves| (A2's 'er_day'); ADX14; choppiness index.
concepts.phone: yes: from index candles
concepts.use: Use trend rules in trends and fade rules in ranges.
pitfalls: You know the regime well only after it is over.

research.finding: None beat random skipping in both years; the ADX pause cut Liquidity from +1,03,019 to +52,096.
Trend vs range day not predictable (AUC 0.46-0.52).

concepts.role: context or filter only: may make Solo skip or prefer a candidate, never create a trade or pick its side
concepts.r61_result: Not a new R61 input (A2 already has `er_day`, `rv_30m`, `day_range_vs_adr10`); not tested again.

concepts.name: FII / DII flows and participant-wise OI
concepts.what: NSE publishes each evening how many index futures and options each group (client, DII, FII, Pro) holds long and short; FII/DII cash flows are published by exchanges/NSDL.
concepts.formula: R61: FII index-futures long share = long / (long + short) from the PREVIOUS session's participant file (published after 18:30), and its change from the session before.
concepts.phone: yes: MarketRecorder records the participant file daily (after 18:30); DII cash flows not reachable
concepts.use: Follow FII futures positioning as 'smart money'; fade crowded client positioning.
pitfalls: A day late; FII futures positions are often hedges for cash holdings.
Signals that worked for years flipped in the last 12 months (OF1).

research.finding: Follow signals pass in design and fail in the holdout; option-buying rules R0-R3 all lose in the holdout.
0 pass (SPA 0.96); FII flows carry a small real signal that is smaller than option costs; 0 of 160 Liquidity filters.

Each input added alone to A2's 29 changed AUC (design / final): `fii_fut_long_share` -0.0010 / +0.0014, `fii_fut_long_chg` -0.0028 / +0.0003. Verdict: no measurable help out of sample (every AUC change under 0.01; the net changes go both ways and are within what one or two trades swing).

concepts.name: Futures basis / premium
concepts.what: Futures price minus the index: normally positive (interest minus dividends to expiry). An unusual premium or discount is read as positioning.
concepts.formula: R61: synthetic forward from put-call parity at the ATM strike: (K + call - put - index) / index x 10,000 bps. Real futures minutes are in the lake only from Jul 2026.
concepts.phone: yes: ChainAnalytics.syntheticFuture; real basis from the futures quote
concepts.use: Rising premium = long positioning; discount = hedging or short positioning.
pitfalls: Mostly interest and dividends; the 'signal' part is tiny.
Synthetic forward uses last-traded prices that can be minutes apart.

research.finding: Basis change, synthetic premium and real basis all fail; a Liquidity skip filter passed design (q 0.008) and went -Rs 35 a day in the holdout.

concepts.name: Rollover
concepts.what: Near expiry, the share of futures positions moved to the next month, and the price paid to roll.
concepts.formula: Next-month OI / (near + next OI) in the last sessions before expiry. Not built in the brain.
concepts.phone: not available on the phone (needs both futures months' OI history); context only
concepts.use: High rollover with a rising premium = longs carried forward (bullish).
pitfalls: Monthly only; a handful of observations a year.

research.finding: Rollover % and roll cost carry no information.

concepts.role: not a model input (not on the phone)
concepts.r61_result: No R61 input: not available on the phone.

concepts.name: Event days (RBI, Budget, CPI, Fed, expiry)
concepts.what: Scheduled news that moves the market: RBI policy (10:00 IST), the Union Budget (11:00), US FOMC decision and US CPI (after the Indian close, so they hit the next session), India CPI (16:00), and expiry days.
concepts.formula: R61: event_rbi_budget = 1 on an RBI policy or Budget day; post_us_event = 1 on the first NSE session after an FOMC decision or US CPI; other_expiry_today = 1 when another of the four indices expires today (Solo never trades an index on its own expiry day). Calendars pre-listed in r61events.py.
concepts.phone: partly: EventCalendar.kt has RBI and Budget; a static FOMC / US CPI list would need bundling; expiry calendar yes
concepts.use: Avoid or size down before events (IV crush, whipsaw); some trade the post-event trend.
pitfalls: Dates shift (the US 2025 shutdown moved CPI); the app's RBI Aug 2026 date (6 Aug) differs from the research list (7 Aug).
Few event days: every result rests on a handful of sessions.

research.finding: BANKNIFTY moves more on RBI + Budget days (range 1.44% vs 0.98%, 15 vs 359 sessions; q 0.08, holdout confirmed p 0.03 on 7 sessions); US CPI / FOMC: bigger gap, same day range.
0 survivors as trade rules; Budget days 2.1-2.4x range; the session after FOMC gaps more.
The last hour of expiry moves more (0.15% vs 0.10%, p 0.004); expiry rules R21-R37 0 of 52 pass.
